data.raw_text:
ICYMI O/N

IRAN:

Negotiators are pessimistic Iran will bend to meet Trump’s demand to reopen the Strait before his Tuesday-night deadline, paving the way for the U.S. to target Iranian bridges and power plants in a fresh escalation of the war. Some U.S. officials say there is too large a gap to narrow before the 8 p.m deadline. (WSJ)

Regional mediators have told Iran that despite Trump's public threats, Trump was still keen on reaching a cease-fire. The U.S. could even compromise on its demands, they added. Iranian mediators, however, argued that the U.S. would likely use the 45-day period to prepare for further attacks. (WSJ)

Decisions on any negotiations are being run through Iran’s Supreme National Security Council and Ahmed Vahidi, the new head of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, a U.S. official and other Middle Eastern officials said to the WSJ. (WSJ)

"If the president sees a deal is coming together, he'll probably hold off. But only he and he alone makes that decision," a senior administration official told Axios. A defense official said they were "skeptical" there would be any extension this time around. (Axios)

Trump might be the most hawkish person in the top echelons of his administration on Iran, according to a U.S. source who spoke to him several times in recent days. (Axios)

US Vice President JD Vance is on standby, prepared to jump into sensitive negotiations with Iran if backchannel talks advance to the point of a direct meeting with Iranian officials. (Politico)

Iran’s offensive against the US and Israel won’t be affected by the threats of President Trump, state-run Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting reports, citing a spokesman for its joint military command. Trump’s threats “stem from being trapped in a deadlock” and arise from the need to justify “the successive defeats of the US army,” spokesman says. (BBG)

Many Iranians, initially welcoming the war, now fear the regime will emerge hardened or that strikes could cause Iran to become a failed state. (WSJ)

The Pentagon is expanding a list of Iranian energy sites it can target for attacks to include ones that provide fuel and power to both civilians and the military, a likely workaround if the administration is accused of war crimes for striking basic infrastructure. (Politico)

The Israeli military said people in Iran should avoid trains until 9 p.m. Tuesday local time. Riding trains or being near railways “puts your life at risk,” the Israeli military said in a Farsi-language post on X. (WSJ)

The King Fahd Causeway, a bridge linking Saudi Arabia to the island country of Bahrain, was closed amid missile attacks targeting Saudi Arabia’s oil-rich Eastern Region. (WSJ)

One of seven Malaysian-owned commercial vessels stranded in the Strait of Hormuz has been “granted safe passage” and is heading to its destination, Malaysia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said. (BBG)

The U.N. Security Council is expected to vote on Tuesday on a resolution to protect commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, but in significantly watered-down form after veto-wielding China opposed authorizing force, diplomats said. (RTRS)

Britain will on Tuesday host a military planning meeting of more than 40 countries willing to secure safe passage in the Strait of Hormuz after the war in the Middle East ends. (FT)

'How China Helped Iran Cushion the Blow of Sanctions and Fund Its War Machine' WSJ article notes over the past half decade, China has provided Iran with a financial lifeline by buying most of its oil, detailing the methods taken to uphold the trade. (WSJ)

Russian satellites have made dozens of detailed imagery surveys of military facilities and critical sites across the Middle East to help Iran strike U.S. forces and other targets, according to a Ukrainian intelligence assessment. (RTRS)

ENERGY CRISIS:  

Iran has yet to allow a single carrier loaded with liquefied natural gas to pass through the Strait of Hormuz in weeks of war, according to traders cited by Bloomberg involved in the transit, a ban that risks exacerbating global shortages. (BBG)

Airlines across Asia are cutting flights, carrying extra fuel from home airports and adding refuelling stops as the Middle East conflict squeezes jet fuel supply in some countries, adding to pressure on an industry already hit by a sharp jump in fuel costs. (RTRS)

India is set to import the most oil from Venezuela in almost six years, helping the world’s third-largest crude importer replace Middle East grades disrupted by the Iran war. (BBG)

Nigeria doubled crude supply to Dangote Refinery in March as Africa’s top oil producer moved to shore up fuel availability after the Iran war disrupted Middle East shipments. (BBG)

China raises domestic retail gasoline, diesel prices again. To mitigate the impact of rising international oil prices on the domestic market, the government is continuing to implement measures to control refined oil prices, the NDRC said. (RTRS)

Chinese coal companies are turning to chemicals manufacturing for growth, as war in the Persian Gulf constrains supply of the liquid fossil fuels more commonly used by the industry. (BBG)

Japan's PM Takaichi said she had no immediate plans to ask households and businesses to cut energy use in ways that would hurt economic activity, despite supply concerns triggered by the war in Iran. (RTRS)

Taiwan will increase coal-fired power generation to bolster energy security, as the war in the Middle East crimps gas supplies. (BBG)

Singapore unveiled around S$1 billion ($778 million) in enhanced support measures to cushion households and businesses from higher energy costs triggered by the war in Iran. (BBG)

The cost of gasoline fell from record levels in Australia, as government measures helped ease some of the pain at the pump caused by the war in the Middle East. (BBG)

Brazil’s government will expand federal tax cuts and subsidies on fuels as it attempts to shield consumers from rising prices due to the war in Iran, broadening measures it had previously unveiled amid the conflict. (BBG)

MACRO:

Goldman Sachs says a reliance on stickier, more patient institutional investors, rather than wealthy individuals, helped its $15.7 billion private credit fund narrowly escape the broader exodus plaguing peers this year. (BBG)

Copper is vulnerable to further declines if the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked, Goldman Sachs warned. (BBG)

Japan’s auction of 30-year notes saw muted demand as investors stayed cautious amid uncertainty about Middle East tensions. (BBG)

Japanese household spending in February fell 1.8% from a year earlier, internal affairs ministry data showed on Tuesday, versus the median market forecast for a 0.7% fall. (RTRS)

The BoJ will likely raise interest rates by July, as soaring oil costs from the Middle East war increase the risk it will fall behind the curve in dealing with mounting inflationary pressure, its former board member Seiji Adachi said on Tuesday. (RTRS)

Japanese Finance Minister Katayama said on Tuesday that the government would stay in close contact with other Group of Seven countries as uncertainties over the Middle East conflict have kept financial markets highly volatile. (RTRS)

China’s resilience to the economic impact of the Iran war and a burgeoning domestic recovery offer the potential for the yuan to break out of a seasonal pattern for losses in the second quarter, according to analysts. (BBG)

Chinese investors should focus on opportunities to position themselves in the A-share market with a “China-centric” investment approach as the Iran war potentially de-escalates this month and the market gradually returns to normal, the Shanghai Securities News reports, citing analysts. (Shanghai Securities News)

New EU cross-border banking rules could hit the City of London, damage European rearmament efforts and undermine PM Starmer’s push to reverse the effects of Brexit, senior financial figures have warned. (FT)

UK pubs and restaurants say they could be forced to cut staff and reduce trading hours, as higher energy prices add to a barrage of rising costs facing the sector. (FT)

Australian household spending rose for a second month in February driven by demand for food, travel and concerts, data showed on Tuesday, though that preceded a global spike in energy costs that will distort consumption for some time to come. (RTRS)

Swedish consumer prices rose much less than expected in March and showed little sign of being affected by the rise in oil prices so far, preliminary data from the statistics office showed on Tuesday. (RTRS)

Czech inflation accelerated less than expected and remained below the official target as the central bank seeks to assess the broader impact of more expensive fuels on cost of living and economic growth. (BBG)

The cost of hedging against swings in a key Indian banking gauge relative to the broader market has surged, as traders brace for the central bank’s rate decision as well as a potential escalation in the Middle East war. (BBG)

The Philippines’ annual inflation rate accelerated more than expected in March, breaching the central bank’s 2% to 4% target range, driven largely by a sharp increase in fuel prices amid escalating tensions in the Middle East. (RTRS)

Indonesian market reforms to meet MSCI Inc.’s demands may stave off a downgrade though they don’t go far enough to prevent a lower weighting in global indexes, some analysts said. (BBG)

GEOPOLITICAL:

Taiwan’s opposition leader is set to arrive in China on Tuesday on what she has called a “historic journey for peace” as she hopes for a face-to-face meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, the first such contact in a decade. (FT)

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un offered rare praise for South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, state media reported, after Lee expressed regret over an incident in which South Korean citizens sent drones over the border into the North’s airspace. (BBG)

EQUITIES:

Bill Ackman’s Pershing Square Capital said it offered to buy Universal Music Group with a bid valuing it at more than 55 billion euros ($63.48 billion). (WSJ)

Rivals OpenAI, Anthropic PBC, and Alphabet Inc.’s Google have begun working together to try to clamp down on Chinese competitors extracting results from cutting-edge US artificial intelligence models to gain an edge in the global AI race. (BBG)

Samsung Electronics, in preliminary results, forecast a more than eightfold jump in first-quarter operating profit, signaling continued record earnings amid the artificial-intelligence boom despite uncertainties fueled by the Middle East conflict. (WSJ)

Broadcom will develop and supply custom artificial-intelligence chips for Google and additional computing capacity to Anthropic in an expansion of the strategic collaboration between the three companies. (WSJ) 

OpenAI urged the attorneys general of California and Delaware to investigate potential “improper and anti-competitive behavior” by Elon Musk in his efforts to block OpenAI from restructuring as a for-profit company. (BBG)

Kalshi won a victory in the battle over who gets to oversee fast-growing prediction markets, after a panel of judges told New Jersey state officials that the Commodity Futures Trading Commission regulates the platform. (BBG)

Phillips 66 estimated nearly $1 billion in losses from its short position in oil and other related commodity derivative contracts in the first quarter as the war in Iran sent crude and fuel prices skyrocketing. (BBG)

Anthropic is planning to invest $200 million in a new venture with major private-equity firms that aims to sell AI tools to their portfolio companies, continuing a push for business customers. (WSJ)

Amazon and the U.S. Postal Service have reached a new package-handling agreement, according to WSJ sources, after Amazon threatened to drastically cut back on the number of packages it sends through the struggling agency. (WSJ)

LG Electronics projected a solid earnings rebound, driven by record first-quarter revenue and improving profitability in its home-appliance, television and vehicle-component businesses. (WSJ)

CATL has tapped the founder and ex-chairman of Zijin Mining Group Co. Ltd. as an advisor for its growing mining business, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

DATA RECAP (Newsquawk):

Australian Balance of Trade (Feb) 5.686B vs. Exp. 2.5B (Prev. 2.631B)
Australian Exports M/M (Feb) 4.9% (Prev. -0.9%)
Australian Imports M/M (Feb) -3.2% (Prev. 0.8%)
French Budget Balance (Feb) -32.1B (Prev. -9.7B)
Indian HSBC Manufacturing PMI Final (Mar) 53.9 vs. Exp. 55.4 (Prev. 56.9)
Japanese Foreign Bond Investment (Mar/28) -945.4
Japanese Monetary Base Y/Y (Mar) -11.6% (Prev. -10.6%)
Japanese Stock Investment by Foreigners (Mar/28) -4448.1
Swiss Inflation Rate M/M (Mar) 0.2% vs. Exp. 0.5% (Prev. 0.6%)
Swiss Inflation Rate Y/Y (Mar) 0.3% vs. Exp. 0.6% (Prev. 0.1%)
